title: Handley Page Halifax JP137
memorial_details:
Stone of remembrance with a triangular pediment set on a marble base with two miliary badges centrally and the lettering in white.

Living Stones, the stonemasons at Tapper Funeral Services in Moordown, made and installed the stone at less than cost.

On 10 July 2011 the memorial was dedicated less than 25 metres from where the aircraft fell.
inscription:
MOORDOWN
HALIFAX MEMORIAL
IN MEMORY OF THE TWO LOCAL RESIDENTS
AND SEVEN AIRCREW WHO LOST THEIR LIVES
IN THE CAUSE OF FREEDOM
WHEN RAF HALIFAX BOMBER JP 137 CRASHED
AT THIS LOCATION ON 21st MARCH 1944
Mrs. DOROTHEA BENNETT Flat 9 Meadow Court
Mr. PERCY F. CHISLETT 1027 Wimborne Road
Sgt. DENIS R. EVANS Pilot RAFVR
Sgt. HENRY W. ROBERTS Nav. RAFVR
F/O STANLEY A. APPLETON B/A RAFVR
Sgt. GEORGE A. ALEXANDER W/Op. RAFVR
Sgt. STANLEY F. GENT F/E RAFVR
Sgt. KENNETH GREEN A/G RAFVR
Sgt. REGINALD R. McGREGOR A/G RCAF
'LEST WE FORGET'
ORGANISED BY THE MOORDOWN 2010 COMMITTEE

narrative:
In the early hours of 21 March 1944, Halifax II JP137 took off from RAF Hurn on a transfer flight to North Africa with No. 3 Overseas Aircraft Dispatch Unit. It was almost new, and heavily laden with fuel for the long flight and more than a ton of supplies. Local research suggests the crew had been picked for special duties with the Special Operations Executive, probably joining 624 Squadron in Algeria.

About two minutes after take-off, at roughly 300 feet, the port wing was seen to drop. Several eyewitnesses saw an engine on fire. JP137 still had the early triangular tail fins, which secret tests at Boscombe Down had shown could overbalance and lock the rudder. With an engine gone, a full load and no height to spare, the aircraft fell into a spin. It clipped the bus depot, came down upside down behind Meadow Court, and slid into the back of the cottages at 1025 to 1031 Wimborne Road before the fuel tanks exploded. The whole flight lasted about three minutes.

All seven crew were killed. The pilot, Sgt Denis Evans, was 20. Two people died in their homes: Dorothea Bennett, 59, a pharmacist's widow, in her back bedroom at 9 Meadow Court, and Percy Chislett, 49, a painter and decorator, in his bedroom at 1027 Wimborne Road. Her daughter Margaret, a young RAMC doctor, escaped through the front of the flat. Percy's wife Mary and son John climbed out of an upstairs window in their nightclothes. Four families lost their homes to the fire.

For decades the Evans family believed Denis had been blamed for the crash. When the Moordown 2010 Committee studied the official papers, they found no real blame had been attached to him beyond the stock wording used when there were no survivors. In January 2012 the head of the RAF Air Historical Branch confirmed this, and the committee formally told the family that Denis was not to blame.

external_narratives.summary: How the three-minute flight unfolded: the dropped port wing at 300 ft, eyewitness reports of an engine fire, and the likely track to Moordown.

Port wing 'seen to drop' about two minutes after take-off, per the AM1180 record card
Several eyewitnesses reported an engine on fire; the official papers do not mention it
Aircraft probably struck the ground inverted after a stall spin

external_narratives.summary: Why the Halifax II's triangular tail fins were dangerous, and how that sealed JP137's fate once an engine failed.

The Mk III Halifax got larger rectangular fins and Hercules engines
JP137 was almost new but still had the early fins

community_connection: The memorial exists because Moordown wanted to give something to Bournemouth's bicentenary in 2010. The Moordown 2010 Committee was formed to find that contribution, and chose to remember the night JP137 came down. Its vice-chairman, David Atkinson, MP for Bournemouth East for 28 years, sketched the design himself. The committee traced the families of all nine victims, including Dr Margaret Bennett, then 96, who still remembered the night. It found photographs and war graves certificates for all seven crew. Evelyn Cleverly OBE, sister of the navigator Henry Roberts, spoke for the families: "This is a personal one, which we shall all cherish so much." The committee's research, photographs, documents and film of the dedication are kept at jp137.com, part of the Moordown Local History Society's pages. The 70th and 80th anniversaries have both been marked at the stone.
crew_summary: 7 crew, all killed, and 2 Moordown residents killed on the ground
cause_of_loss: Loss of control shortly after take-off from RAF Hurn. Eyewitnesses reported an engine on fire (not in the official papers); local research points to rudder overbalance from the Halifax II's triangular tail fins

maintainer.notes: The memorial was commissioned and dedicated by the Moordown 2010 Committee. Its research and records are published at jp137.com alongside the Moordown Local History Society pages, which take enquiries through a contact form. Moordown is unparished; the local authority is BCP Council (Moordown ward).
